title: Hearing Louis Armstrong's records
summary: He bought Louis Armstrong's records, including 'Sleepy Time Down South' and the Hot Five instrumentals, and played along.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, listen, well, by the time that you were in Dallas, playing with this band and everything, you must have heard Louis on records.
Oh, sure, yes.
Well, you must have gotten a terrific shock when you heard that, didn't you? Did that knock you out?
His 'Sleepy Time Down South' was one of them. And I think it was 'Firecracker' or 'Fireworks' that came out.
Oh, I know the one you're talking about.
One of his big hits.
Yeah. The instrumentals, the five pieces.
Right.
Earl and Zuttie and --
That used to just slay me, because I ruin (unintelligible) records.
"Cornet" and Part of Chop Suey in those.
Right, right, right. Well, that band just knocked me out.
Yeah.
And I was just playing right along with it.
Did you still not have any phonograph at all?
Oh, yes, at home, I had one then, in Dallas, sure, yeah.
And then did you get to buy a few records?
Oh, yes, yes, I bought all those records.
You did?
Even "Five foot two, eyes of blue," --
Oh, yeah.
That's another thing.
